query: AlCrFeNiSi belongs to a high-entropy-alloy family developed to combine properties that traditional single-principal-element alloys often cannot achieve simultaneously. Earlier research sought stable solid solutions and adjusted HEA compositions to target particular properties, but tradeoffs persisted: the CoCrFeMnNi system has limited wear and corrosion resistance, manganese can promote oxidation and oxide spallation, and cobalt-containing systems raise cost and processability concerns. Conventional bulk fabrication can cause compositional segregation during cooling, whereas mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing techniques can generate residual thermal stresses that impair mechanical performance and increase processing complexity. Given cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock, what single intervention could improve mechanical integrity while limiting segregation, residual stress, and defect formation? State one hypothesis containing the intervention, its causal mechanism, a quantitative or directional outcome relative to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi, the processing and test boundaries of validity, the prior evidence supporting it, and a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a controlled substrate preheating step during laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) processing of cobalt‐free AlCrFeNiSi alloy powders will reduce residual thermal gradients, limit compositional segregation and defect formation, and thereby improve the overall mechanical integrity of the fabricated parts.
generation.material_initial_state: Cobalt‐free AlCrFeNiSi high‐entropy alloy powder produced by conventional atomization methods, which in standard LPBF processing shows microsegregation, residual stresses, and defects.
generation.intervention: Implement substrate/chamber preheating (e.g., to 200–300 °C) during the LPBF process while holding other laser parameters constant.
generation.conditions: LPBF processing using optimized laser power and scan speed for full density; preheating is applied within temperature bounds that do not alter powder chemistry or phase stability; tests conducted under comparable ambient conditions to conventional processing.
generation.structural_mediator: A reduced thermal gradient during solidification leading to a more uniform melt pool cooling and refined grain structure with less phase segregation and diminished thermal stress accumulation.
generation.mechanism: Preheating the build substrate lowers the temperature differential between the melt pool and the substrate. This diminished thermal gradient reduces rapid cooling and heterogeneous nucleation that normally promote compositional segregation and high residual stress. Consequently, microstructural defects (e.g., hot cracks) are minimized and the overall homogeneity and mechanical robustness of the alloy are enhanced.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi parts (without preheating), the preheated samples are predicted to exhibit lower residual stress levels, reduced segregation and defect densities, and improved mechanical properties such as higher tensile strength and ductility.
generation.baseline: Conventional LPBF processing of AlCrFeNiSi without substrate preheating typically results in significant compositional segregation during rapid cooling, elevated residual thermal stresses, and increased formation of processing-induced defects.
generation.boundary: This intervention is anticipated to be effective for cobalt‐free AlCrFeNiSi processed by LPBF under similar powder characteristics and laser parameters; its applicability to other HEA systems or extreme preheat temperatures remains to be verified.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal preheating temperature range and its exact quantitative impact on mechanical property enhancement need further empirical determination; interplay with other LPBF parameters (e.g., laser power, scan speed) may introduce variability.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of AlCrFeNiSi samples via LPBF using the same powder feedstock and process parameters. One set is processed with substrate preheating (200–300 °C) and the other without any preheating. Ensure identical scanning, layering, and laser energy input for both groups.
measurements: Residual stress measurement using X-ray diffraction
Microstructural analysis by SEM/EBSD for grain size and phase homogeneity
Defect density quantification (e.g., crack and pore analysis)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the preheated samples do not demonstrate statistically significant improvements in lower residual stresses, reduced segregation/defect density, and enhanced mechanical properties relative to the non‐preheated control group, then the hypothesis is invalidated.

Laser Powder Bed Fusion Additive Manufacturing of a CoCrFeNiCu High-Entropy Alloy: Processability, Microstructural Insights, and (In Situ) Mechanical Behavior

Abstract: AbstractHigh-entropy alloys are known for their promising mechanical properties, wear and corrosion resistance, which are maintained across a wide range of temperatures. In this study, a CoCrFeNiCu-based high-entropy alloy, distinguished from conventional CoCrFeNi systems by the addition of Cu, which is known to enhance toughness and wear resistance, was investigated to better understand the effects of compositional modification on processability and performance. Microstructural Evolution of AlCoCrFeNiSi High-Entropy Alloy Powder during Mechanical Alloying and Its Coating Performance

Abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) are promising structural materials due to their excellent comprehensive performances. The use of mechanically alloyed powders to deposit HEA coatings through atmospheric plasma spraying (APS) is an effective approach that can broaden the application areas of the HEAs. In this paper, a ductility–brittleness AlCoCrFeNiSi system was chosen as an object of study, and the detailed evolution of the surface morphology, particle size distribution, and microstructure of the powder during mechanical alloying was investigated. An AlCoCrFeNiSi HEA coating was deposited using powder milled for 10 h, which can be used as an ideal feedstock for APS. The surface morphology, microstructure, microhardness, and wear behavior of the coating at room temperature were investigated. The results showed that as the milling time increased, the particle size first increased, and then decreased.
